source.title: Level-raising and symmetric power functoriality, III
source.authors: Laurent Clozel and Jack A. Thorne
source.version: The accepted manuscript, dated 10 December 2015 (53 pages; the version deposited as 'Accepted version' in the Cambridge repository, identical in text to the copy on the second author's homepage), read in full. The paper is not on arXiv, and the published Duke article (78 pages) could not be accessed, so locators give accepted-manuscript page numbers and the source issues were not checked against the published text. The introduction thanks 'all the referees', so the manuscript postdates refereeing. Review (REV-PAPER-CLOZEL-THORNE-17, Claude Code, session cc-38267a, 23 September 2026): the repository copy (SHA-256 fb88e83c3c056c2fa6100d1fbb4d0853c4ec636cc68a33548ac4259336094742) was read in full against its page images by three checkers (§§1–2, §§3–4, §§5–7); the coordinator re-derived the substantive findings. The published Duke text was again not accessible.

summary: Clozel and Thorne prove that the 6th and 8th symmetric powers of a non-CM cuspidal representation π of GL_2(A_F) attached to a Hilbert modular form exist, for F totally real and linearly disjoint from Q(ζ_5), resp. Q(ζ_7) (Theorem 6.1). With their earlier papers and a reduction for forms of mixed parity (§7) this gives Sym^n π for n ≤ 8 when F ∩ Q(ζ_35) = Q (Corollary 7.2), and the holomorphy of L(Sym^n π, s). The key is the congruence Sym^{l+1} r̄ ≅ (φr̄ ⊗ r̄) ⊕ χ²Sym^{l−3} r̄ for l = 5, 7: the residual representation is endoscopic of type (4, l − 2), so a Steinberg lift of it must be produced before Thorne's automorphy lifting for residually reducible representations applies. They construct Iwahori-spherical representations of ramified unitary groups by Kazhdan–Lusztig, place them in Mœglin–Mok L-packets and study their integral structures (§§2–3). They count automorphic representations of a definite unitary group with endoscopic base change (Theorem 3.8), raise the level with algebraic modular forms and a pairing argument that works only for l = 5, 7 (Theorem 4.2), and raise it further to Steinberg by deformation theory of reducible residual representations (Theorem 5.1, giving the automorphy lifting Theorem 5.7). In the atlas the endpoints belong to ModularityAndLanglandsExtensions ML.3, which receives the final theorems and the §7 reductions as a source route. The level-raising method is planned nowhere and becomes a Part II of that roadmap. Casselman's lemma, the Iwahori–Matsumoto and Bernstein–Lusztig presentations and Kazhdan–Lusztig go as sources to SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups SR.1–SR.3, and the partition deformation rings R^m_v to LocalGaloisDeformationRings L7. Mok's classification (ML.4), the known transfers (ML.5), unitary trace formulas (ET.4/ET.7), buildings (RG2.2/RG2.4) and the attached Galois representations (AG2.x) are planned. Five misprints are recorded; no stated result is affected. After review (REV-PAPER-CLOZEL-THORNE-17): 81 items (0 library, 17 planned, 64 missing) and 8 routes. Thorne 2015's inputs, ι-ordinarity, [CT14] and BLGGT14 Theorem 4.2.1 moved to PolarizedAutomorphyLifting (route 5), the Iwahori–Hecke presentations and Kazhdan–Lusztig's classification to SmoothRepresentationsPartIIParahoricCenters (route 6), the congruence (1.1) to ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations G7 (route 7), and [CHT08, Lemma 4.1.4] and coefficient conjugation to AutomorphicGaloisRepresentationsPartII (route 8), matching the Newton–Thorne extractions. Source issues: E1–E5 are confirmed and E6–E23 are new. The substantive ones are E7 (a wrong entry in the n = 9 Hecke matrix, which as printed does not define a module), E8 (Theorem 2.4(a) misstated), E10 (a false uniqueness claim in §3.5), E20 (primitivity of r_{𝔭₀} unproved), E21 (Lemma 5.3 proved only for unipotent conditions), E22 (Theorem 6.2 lacks a hypothesis needed for Theorem 5.7) and E23 (the descent in Theorem 7.1 is ambiguous up to η_{E/F}). All have direct repairs, and none affects Theorem 1.1 or Corollaries 1.2–1.3 under their stated hypotheses.

items.name: Existence of the n-th symmetric power lift Sym^n π
items.statement: Let F be a totally real field and π a cuspidal automorphic representation of GL_2(A_F) attached to a classical Hilbert modular form (weights ≥ 2, constant parity) that is not of CM type. Sym^n π exists if there is a regular algebraic cuspidal automorphic representation Π of GL_{n+1}(A_F) with Sym^n r_l(π) ≅ r_l(Π) for every prime l (for one, hence every, embedding of the coefficient field into Q̄_l); for mixed-parity π (§7) the condition is Sym^n rec_{F_v}(π_v) ≅ rec_{F_v}(Π_v) at every finite place v.
items.note: ML.0 plans the endpoint and normalisation registry and ML.3 the symmetric-power endpoints; this Galois-theoretic definition is the form of the endpoint the Clozel–Thorne series proves.

items.name: Conventions of [CT14, §2]: RACSDC, RAESDC and RACSD representations, ι-ordinarity, weight and infinity type, and r_ι(π)
items.statement: For a CM or totally real field, regular algebraic (essentially) conjugate self-dual cuspidal automorphic representations of GL_n (RACSDC, RAESDC, RAECSDC, RACSD), the weight λ ∈ (Z^n_+)^{Hom(E,C)} and infinity type a of a regular algebraic cuspidal representation, the local Langlands correspondences rec_{F_v}, rec^T_{F_v} for GL_n, the attached Galois representations r_ι(π): G_F → GL_n(Q̄_l), and what it means for a Galois representation to be automorphic.
items.note: AutomorphicGaloisRepresentationsPartII AG2.0 plans weights and normalisations and AG2.2 the polarized Galois systems; PotentialAutomorphyInfrastructure PA.2 the ordinary GL_n theory over CM fields; EndoscopicTransfer ET.6 the local Langlands correspondence for GL_n. Review (REV-PAPER-CLOZEL-THORNE-17): PotentialAutomorphyInfrastructure PA.2 was removed from the planned layers: it plans ordinary parts in the unpolarized ACC+ setting, not ι-ordinarity of RACSDC representations, which is now item 057, routed to PolarizedAutomorphyLifting as in the three Newton–Thorne extractions. §1.1 names RACSDC, RAESDC and RACSD; RAECSDC is used later.

items.name: Galois representations attached to RACSDC representations, with local–global compatibility including monodromy
items.statement: For a RACSDC automorphic representation Π of GL_n(A_E) (E CM) and ι: Q̄_l ≅ C there is a continuous semisimple r_ι(Π): G_E → GL_n(Q̄_l) with r_ι(Π)^c ≅ r_ι(Π)^∨ ε^{1−n}, and for every finite place w ∤ l, WD(r_ι(Π)|_{G_{E_w}})^{F-ss} ≅ rec^T_{E_w}(Π_w) (Taylor–Yoshida), used with the Jordan decomposition of the monodromy operator N.
items.locator: Used in Proposition 4.1, p. 34, Theorem 5.1, p. 37, and Theorem 5.7, p. 44
items.note: AG2.5 plans 'the Caraiani/Taylor–Yoshida upgrades' with full monodromy comparison. Review (REV-PAPER-CLOZEL-THORNE-17): full local–global compatibility with monodromy at every w ∤ l for all RACSDC Π is due to Caraiani (Duke 2012), beyond the Taylor–Yoshida case the paper cites; purity of r_ι(Π)|G_{E_w} (used in Lemmas 5.2 and 5.4) comes with it. AG2.5 plans 'the Caraiani/Taylor–Yoshida upgrades'.

items.name: The ramified unitary group U_n, its building and the parahoric subgroups B ⊃ Iwahori and P
items.statement: Let p be odd, F/Q_p finite, E/F ramified quadratic with uniformiser ϖ, ϖ² ∈ F, v(ϖ) = ½, n = 2k + 1, and U_n(R) = {g ∈ GL_n(R ⊗_{O_F} O_E) : ᵗg J g^c = J} with J antidiagonal. The maximal split torus S has non-reduced relative root system BC_k; Z = Z_{U_n}(S), Λ = Z/Z_c ≅ Z^k with basis ε_1, …, ε_k. The standard apartment, affine roots {a_ij + ½Z} ∪ {a_i + ½Z} ∪ {2a_i + ½ + Z}, the chamber C: 0 < a_k < ⋯ < a_1 < ¼ with simple affine roots α_0 = 2a_{−1} + ½, a_{1,−2}, …, a_k, and the affine Weyl group W = W_0 ⋉ Λ of type B_k generated by s_0, …, s_k (with s_0 given by (2.1)). K = U_n(O_F) is special; B = U_n^C is the preimage of the upper-triangular subgroup of O(J)(k_F) and contains an Iwahori subgroup with index 2; P = U_n^F is the preimage of block upper-triangular matrices with a 3 × 3 middle block, [P : B] = q + 1. (U_n, B, N) is a Tits system.
items.note: ReductiveGroupsPartII RG2.2 plans Bruhat–Tits buildings with facets and fixers, and RG2.4 the Iwahori–Bruhat decomposition with non-split examples. Tau Ceti has the abstract Tits system (TauCeti.TitsSystem, TauCeti/GroupTheory/TitsSystem/Basic.lean:48) and its Bruhat decomposition, but not buildings or parahorics. Corrected for source issue E1 (the paper prints Λ ≅ Z^m). Review (REV-PAPER-CLOZEL-THORNE-17): the paper calls W 'an affine Coxeter group of type B_k' (p. 6); its Coxeter diagram is that of type C̃_k (s₀s₁ and s_{k−1}s_k have order 4), with W₀ of type B_k = C_k. The rest was checked (chamber, root basis, (2.1), [P : B] = q + 1, index 2).

items.name: Lemma 2.1: invariants of B and P through Jacquet modules (Casselman)
items.statement: For an admissible C[U_n]-module π there are canonical isomorphisms π^B ≅ (π_{N_0})^{Z_c} and π^P ≅ (π_{N_P})^{M∩P} (unnormalised Jacquet modules).
items.note: The first is Casselman's Proposition 2.4 (1980); the second follows as in [CT15, Proposition 2.1].

items.name: The Iwahori–Matsumoto presentation of the Hecke algebra of a Tits system
items.statement: For a Tits system (G, B, N) whose Weyl group (W, Σ) is a Coxeter system with q_w = #BwB/B = q^{l(w)}, the convolution algebra H_B of compactly supported B-biinvariant Z-valued functions (vol(B) = 1) is free on the double cosets [BwB] and isomorphic to Z[B_W]/((T_s − q)(T_s + 1) : s ∈ Σ), B_W the braid group, via [BwB] ↦ T_w (Matsumoto 1964).
items.note: Mathlib has CoxeterSystem and its length function (Mathlib/GroupTheory/Coxeter/Basic.lean:157, Mathlib/GroupTheory/Coxeter/Length.lean:75); Tau Ceti has Tits systems and an abstract double-coset Hecke ring (TauCeti/NumberTheory/HeckeRing/) but not this presentation. Review (REV-PAPER-CLOZEL-THORNE-17): the paper prints the relation (T_s − 1)(T_s + q) = 0 (p. 7), and the item copied it. With T_s = [BsB] one has T_s² = q + (q − 1)T_s, so the relation is (T_s − q)(T_s + 1) = 0, as the paper's own Lusztig relation on p. 8 and all its Hecke matrices confirm (sourceIssues E6).

items.name: Proposition 2.2: H_B ≅ H_{B'}, the Iwahori–Hecke algebra of Sp_{2k}
items.statement: Let B' be the Iwahori subgroup of the split group Sp_{2k}(F) and Λ' ≅ Z^k with basis ε'_i = diag(1, …, ϖ², …, ϖ^{−2}, …, 1). The identifications Λ ≅ Λ', W_0 ≅ W'_0 extend to W ≅ W' carrying {s_0, …, s_k} to the simple affine reflections of Sp_{2k}, and induce an isomorphism of Hecke algebras H_B ≅ H_{B'} with [Bε_iB] ↦ [B'ε'_iB'].

items.name: The Bernstein–Lusztig presentation H_{B,C} = H_0 ⊗̃ C[X]
items.statement: With the based root datum of SO_{2k+1}(C) (X = Λ, simple roots ε_i − ε_{i+1}, ε_k), H_{B,C} is the twisted tensor product of H_0 = ⟨T_w : w ∈ W_0⟩ and C[X], with θB_s = B_sθ^s + (θ^s − θ)ζ_β for a simple root β, s = s_β, B_s = T_s − q, where ζ_β = (q − e^β)/(1 − e^β) for β long and (q − e^β)(1 + e^β)/(1 − e^{2β}) otherwise (Lusztig 1989, §3). Its commutative subalgebra O[Λ] acts on Iwahori invariants through the exponents of the Jacquet module.

items.name: The parameter φ_E of Π_E = St_{n−4,E} ⊞ St_{3,E} ⊞ St_{1,E}, exponents, and its L-packet Π_φ
items.statement: For n ≥ 7 let Π_E = St_{n−4,E} ⊞ St_{3,E} ⊞ St_{1,E}, a tempered representation of GL_n(E), with conjugate orthogonal parameter φ_E, and φ its unique extension to a parameter of U_n; Π_φ is the corresponding L-packet. An exponent [m_1, …, m_k] is the character |·|^{m_1} ⊗ ⋯ ⊗ |·|^{m_k} ⊗ 1 of the torus (E^×)^k × (E^×)^{N=1}; (·)^norm_{N_0} is the normalised Jacquet module for the upper-triangular Borel. f_E ↦ f is the transfer of test functions for stable base change and I_θ: Π_E ≅ Π_E^c the Whittaker-normalised intertwining operator.

items.name: Theorem 2.3(1): the L-packet for n = 7
items.statement: In the setting of item 009, for n = 7, Π_φ has exactly two elements X, Y, characterised by: (a) ⟨tr X + tr Y, f⟩ = ⟨tr Π_E × I_θ, f_E⟩; (b) dim X^P = dim X^B = 1, dim Y^B = 7; (c) X^norm_{N_0} = [1, 0, −1] and (Y^norm_{N_0})^ss = [1, 0, −1] + 2[1, 0, 1] + 4[1, 1, 0].
items.locator: Theorem 2.3, accepted manuscript pp. 8–9; part 1; proved in §3.5, pp. 24–28
items.note: Review (REV-PAPER-CLOZEL-THORNE-17): locator: the heading of Theorem 2.3 is on p. 8, parts (a)–(c) on p. 9.

items.name: Theorem 2.3(2): the L-packet for n = 9
items.statement: For n = 9, Π_φ is a discrete L-packet with exactly four elements X, Y, Z, W, characterised by: (a) ⟨tr X + tr Y + tr Z + tr W, f⟩ = ⟨tr Π_E × I_θ, f_E⟩; (b) dim X^P = dim X^B = 1, dim Y^B = 11, dim Z^B = 2, dim W^B = 0; (c) X^norm_{N_0} = [2, 1, 0, −1], (Y^norm_{N_0})^ss = [2, 1, 0, −1] + 2[2, 1, 0, 1] + 4[2, 1, 1, 0] + [1, 0, 2, 1] + [1, 2, 0, 1] + 2[1, 2, 1, 0], (Z^norm_{N_0})^ss = [1, 0, 2, 1] + [1, 2, 0, 1].
items.note: Review (REV-PAPER-CLOZEL-THORNE-17): locator: the heading of Theorem 2.3 is on p. 8, parts (a)–(c) on p. 9.

items.name: Theorem 2.3(3): the L-packets for n = 2k + 1 ≥ 11, inductively
items.statement: For n = 2k + 1 ≥ 11, Π_φ is a discrete L-packet with exactly four elements X_k, Y_k, Z_k, W_k characterised by the trace identity, dim X_k^P = dim X_k^B = 1, dim Y_k^B = dim Y_{k−1}^B + k, dim Z_k^B = dim Z_{k−1}^B + (k − 2), dim W_k^B = 0, and: X_k^norm = [k − 2, k − 3, …, 0, −1]; (Y_k^norm)^ss is the sum of the exponents [1, k − 2, k − 3, …, 1] with 0 inserted as the i-th entry (i = 2, …, k − 1), the exponent 2[1, k − 2, …, 1, 0], and the exponents of Y_{k−1} with k − 2 inserted first; (Z_k^norm)^ss the same without the term 2[1, k − 2, …, 1, 0], with Z_{k−1} in place of Y_{k−1}.
items.note: Review (REV-PAPER-CLOZEL-THORNE-17): locator: the heading of Theorem 2.3 is on p. 8, parts (a)–(c) on p. 9.

items.name: Theorem 2.4: Kazhdan–Lusztig's Deligne–Langlands classification of tempered Iwahori-spherical representations
items.statement: Let G be a split reductive group over F with connected centre and I an Iwahori subgroup. The tempered irreducible π with π^I ≠ 0 are in natural bijection with Ĝ-conjugacy classes of triples (s, u, ρ) with u ∈ Ĝ unipotent, s ∈ Ĝ semisimple with sus^{−1} = u^q and of the tempered form s = s_c·φ(diag(q^{1/2}, q^{−1/2})) for a homomorphism φ : SL₂(C) → Ĝ with φ(unipotent upper triangular) = u and s_c in a compact subgroup of Z_Ĝ(φ), and ρ an irreducible representation of M̄(u, s) = π₀((Z_Ĝ(s) ∩ Z_Ĝ(u))/Z_Ĝ) occurring in H_*(B^s_u, C), B^s_u the variety of Borel subgroups containing s and u (Kazhdan–Lusztig 1987, Theorems 7.12 and 8.2).
items.locator: Theorem 2.4, accepted manuscript pp. 9–10; Kazhdan–Lusztig 1987, Theorems 7.12 and 8.2
items.note: A deep theorem (equivariant K-theory of Steinberg varieties); stated as an input. The homology description is in Chriss–Ginzburg, Ch. 8. Review (REV-PAPER-CLOZEL-THORNE-17): condition (a) is printed as 's is contained in a maximal compact subgroup of Ĝ(C)' (p. 10), which with sus^{−1} = u^q forces u = 1 (Ad(s) would have an eigenvalue q on log u) and would exclude the Steinberg-type parameters the paper uses; the tempered condition of KL87 §8 was restored (sourceIssues E8; the application in Theorem 2.5 has s_c = 1). The Jacquet-module formula the item stated is not part of Theorem 2.4: it is [KL87, §7.6], used in the proof of Theorem 2.5, and is now item 063.

items.name: Theorem 2.5: construction of the Iwahori-spherical modules X, Y, Z by Kazhdan–Lusztig
items.statement: For n = 7 there are irreducible admissible C[U_n]-modules X, Y with the dimensions and Jacquet exponents of Theorem 2.3(1)(b)(c); for n = 9 modules X, Y, Z with those of Theorem 2.3(2)(b)(c) (W excluded); and for n = 2k + 1 ≥ 11 modules X_k, Y_k, Z_k with those of Theorem 2.3(3). They are obtained, through Proposition 2.2, from PSp_{2k}(F)-representations attached by Theorem 2.4 to the partition n = (n − 4) + 3 + 1 of the dual SO_{2k+1}(C): M(u, s) = {±1} (n = 7) or {±1}², and B^s_u is paved by affine spaces (De Concini–Lusztig–Procesi; Białynicki-Birula), with the components and exponents listed in the proof.
items.note: For n = 7, B^s_u = X_1 ⊔ X_2 ⊔ X_3 with X_1 two points (exponent [1, 0, −1]), X_2 ≅ P^1 ([1, 0, 1]) and X_3 ≅ P^1 × P^1 ([1, 1, 0]); H_*(B^s_u) is 8-dimensional. Review (REV-PAPER-CLOZEL-THORNE-17): the Białynicki-Birula paving is used for n = 7; for n ≥ 9 the paper cites [Ree94, pp. 485–486] and [DCLP88, §3.8], with the smoothness of B^D_u from [DCLP88, §3.6]. The paper writes M̄(u, s).

items.name: Proposition 2.6: integral structures with disjoint reductions (q a primitive root mod l)
items.statement: Let l = n − 2 be prime (n ∈ {7, 9}), ι: Q̄_l ≅ C, K/Q_l finite with ring of integers O, residue field k, containing √q, over which X, Y (and Z) are defined. If q is a primitive root modulo l there are H_{B,O}-lattices X^B_O, Y^B_O (and Z^B_O) in X^B_K, Y^B_K (Z^B_K) such that the reductions X^B_O ⊗ k, Y^B_O ⊗ k (and Z^B_O ⊗ k) have pairwise no common Jordan–Hölder factor as H_{B,k}-modules; in fact Y^B_O ⊗ k is absolutely irreducible.
items.locator: Proposition 2.6, accepted manuscript p. 12; Remark 2.7, p. 17
items.note: Y^B_O is given by explicit matrices of T_{s_i} and the ε_i computed with Reeder's Matrices for affine Hecke modules (2000). Remark 2.7: the matrices define Y^B_K without the primitive-root hypothesis; it is needed only for integrality. Review (REV-PAPER-CLOZEL-THORNE-17): the n = 9 matrix T_{s₂} is misprinted: its (10,10) entry must be −1/(1+q), not 1 + q (sourceIssues E7; checked by the quadratic, braid and Bernstein relations). The descent of X, Y, Z to a finite K/Q_l containing √q is [BH06, 4.3, Proposition] (p. 12). Absolute irreducibility of Y^B_O ⊗ k is proved in the proof, not stated.

items.name: Corollary 2.8: lattices in (X^a ⊕ Y^b ⊕ Z^c)^B split into isotypic parts
items.statement: Let q be a primitive root mod l and M a finite flat H_{B,O}-module with M ⊗ K ≅ (X^B_K)^a ⊕ (Y^B_K)^b (n = 7) or (X^B_K)^a ⊕ (Y^B_K)^b ⊕ (Z^B_K)^c (n = 9). With M_X = M ∩ (X^B_K-isotypic part) and so on, the natural map M_X ⊕ M_Y (⊕ M_Z) → M is an isomorphism.
items.note: Review (REV-PAPER-CLOZEL-THORNE-17): the proof also needs Brauer–Nesbitt for H_{B,O}-lattices, to compare the reductions of M_X, M_Y, M_Z with those of the lattices of Proposition 2.6.

items.name: Proposition 2.9: the χ̄-localisations when q ≡ −1 mod l
items.statement: Let χ: O[Λ] → O give the action on X^B_K, χ̄ its reduction, and ȷ the anti-involution [BgB] ↦ [Bg^{−1}B]. Suppose q ≡ −1 mod l. Then X^B_K = X^B_K(χ̄) = X^B_K(χ̄ȷ) and dim_K Y^P_K ∩ Y^B_K(χ̄) = dim_K Y^P_K ∩ Y^B_K(χ̄ȷ) = 1; and for n = 9 also Z^B_K(χ̄) = 0.
items.note: Review (REV-PAPER-CLOZEL-THORNE-17): the anti-involution is written ȷ in the paper, not ‖.

items.name: L-groups of unitary groups, stable and unstable base change of parameters, and bounded parameters
items.statement: For E/F quadratic (local or global) and G = U(n): ᴸG = GL_n(C) ⋊ W_F with c acting by g ↦ Φ_n ᵗg^{−1} Φ_n^{−1}; the L-homomorphism ᴸG → ᴸ(Res_{E/F} G_E), (g, w) ↦ (g, g, w); Φ_bdd(G) the bounded parameters L_F → ᴸG (L_F = W_F or W_F × SU_2(R)). Lemma 3.1: for n odd, φ ↦ φ|_{L_E} is a bijection from Φ_bdd(G) onto the conjugate orthogonal parameters of GL_n(E) (stable base change), and for a character μ of E^× with μ|_{F^×} = ε_{E/F}, φ ↦ φ|_{L_E} ⊗ μ is a bijection onto the conjugate symplectic ones (unstable base change); tempered representations decompose into the L-packets Π_φ (Mœglin, Mok).
items.locator: Lemma 3.1, accepted manuscript p. 19; §§2.2, 3.1, pp. 8, 19; Mok, Lemma 2.2.1
items.note: ML.4 plans Arthur/Mok classification inputs 'with explicit proof-source owners: … packets, multiplicities'.

items.name: The endoscopic group H = U(n − 4) × U(4) and the embedding ξ: ᴸH → ᴸG twisted by μ
items.statement: With m = n − 4 and μ as in Lemma 3.1, ξ sends (g_1, g_2) × 1 to diag(g_1, g_2), 1 × w (w ∈ W_E) to diag(1_m, μ(w)1_4) × w and 1 × w_c to diag(Φ_m, Φ_4)Φ_n^{−1} × w_c (Mínguez); (3.1) is a conjugate form used for the computations.
items.note: Review (REV-PAPER-CLOZEL-THORNE-17): μ is a character E^× → C^× (local) or E^×\A_E^× → C^× (global) with μ|_{F^×} (resp. μ|_{A_F^×}) = ε_{E/F}; the review checked that ξ is an L-homomorphism (ξ(1 × w_c)² = (diag(1_m, −1_4), w_c²) forces μ(w_c²) = −1).

items.name: Theorem 3.2 (Mœglin, Mok): the L-packet of φ_E has two or four elements
items.statement: The parameter φ_E determines an L-packet Π_φ of tempered representations of G = U_n(F): (i) if m = n − 4 = 3 it has two elements X, Y (the two summands of the reducible n-Ind(St_{3,E} ⊗ 1) from the GL_3(E) × U(1) Levi); (ii) if m ≥ 5 it has four elements X, Y, Z, W in the discrete series. S_φ = π_0(S_φ/{±1}) is {±1} in case (i) and {±1}² in case (ii), paired with Π_φ.
items.locator: Theorem 3.2, accepted manuscript p. 20; Mok, Theorem 2.5.1

items.name: Theorem 3.3 with the signs of the packet: identification of X, Y, Z and their Jacquet modules
items.statement: Suppose E/F ramified and the residue characteristic of F odd. Then the members X, Y (m = 3) or X, Y, Z (m ≥ 5) of Π_φ are semistable with the Jacquet exponents of Theorem 2.3 (for m = 3, X has exponent [1, 0, −1] and Y exponents 4[1, 1, 0] + 2[1, 0, 1] + [1, 0, −1]); W is not semistable. With the characters ε_1, ε_2 of S_φ, the sign ε = ε_1ε_2 satisfies ε(Y) = ε(Z) = 1 and ε(X) = ε(W) = −1, and ε_1(X) = ε_1(Y) = 1, ε_1(Z) = ε_1(W) = −1.
items.locator: Theorem 3.3, accepted manuscript p. 21; sign table p. 21; proof in §3.5, pp. 24–28
items.note: Corrected for source issue E3: part (i) prints the exponent of X as [1, 0, 1]. The proof compares the stable identity and the endoscopic identity Σ ε(π)⟨tr π, f⟩ = ⟨tr π_H, f^H⟩ ((3.7)) on the maximal split torus, using Lemma 3.6 and Proposition 3.7. Review (REV-PAPER-CLOZEL-THORNE-17): the sign table is a labelling convention fixed before the theorem (p. 21: 'In case (i) we set ε(X) = −1 …'); the theorem asserts that the members so labelled are semistable with the stated exponents. 'W is not semistable' is proved on p. 26, not stated. The ε values come from (3.7), Lemma 3.6 and the U(4) Jacquet computation (item 066); Proposition 3.7 is needed only for the ε₁ values. The identification of Z in the proof uses a false uniqueness claim (sourceIssues E10), with an immediate repair.

items.name: Lemma 3.4: a conjugate-symplectic Hecke character μ with prescribed archimedean components
items.statement: For a CM extension E/F of a totally real field there is a continuous μ: E^×\A_E^× → C^× with μ|_{A_F^×} = ε_{E/F} and μ(z) = (z/z̄)^{1/2} for z ∈ E_w ≅ C at every archimedean place w.

items.name: Theorem 3.5 (Mok): multiplicity formula for the quasi-split unitary group and the endoscopic datum (Π_m, Π_4 ⊗ μ)
items.statement: Let Π_m, Π_4 be conjugate self-dual cuspidal representations of GL_m(A_E), GL_4(A_E) with the archimedean parameters of §3.3, so that (Π_m, Π_4 ⊗ μ) is a tempered Arthur parameter ψ for the quasi-split G* = U(n) with S_ψ = {±1} ∋ s. For local π_v ∈ Π_{φ_v}, almost all unramified, π = ⊗π_v occurs in L²_cusp(G*(F)\G*(A)) if and only if ∏_v ⟨s, π_v⟩ = 1, and then with multiplicity one.
items.locator: Theorem 3.5, accepted manuscript p. 22; Mok, Theorem 2.5.2
items.note: Mok's results are conditional on the stabilisation of the twisted trace formula (Mœglin–Waldspurger); cuspidality follows because residual representations are nowhere tempered (Clozel 1993).

items.name: Arthur's stabilisation of the trace formula for G* and G, and the reduction to the endoscopic data (G*, H)
items.statement: I^{G*}_disc(f*) = Σ_E ι(G*, E) S^E_disc(f*^E) (3.12) and T^G_disc(f) = I^G_disc(f) = Σ_E ι(G, E) S^E_disc(f^E) (3.13) (Arthur 2003, 2005); by Labesse's CM base change for stable discrete terms and Jacquet–Shalika disjointness (the argument of Clozel–Harris–Labesse 2011, Lemma 4.2), after isolating the Hecke eigenvalues of σ_1 ⊞ σ_2 only E = G* and E = H contribute, and for a cuspidal π only E = G*; the other H-packets are removed by Hodge–Tate weights ([Gue11, Theorem 2.3]) and the Eisenstein terms of I^{G*}_disc by Hecke eigenvalues ([Art05, (21.19)]).
items.locator: Proof of Theorem 3.8, (3.12)–(3.13), accepted manuscript pp. 29–31
items.note: ET.4 plans the simple stable and twisted unitary trace formulas and ET.7 the unitary-to-GL base-change identities; ML.4 the stabilisation inputs. Review (REV-PAPER-CLOZEL-THORNE-17): the two removal steps and the cuspidal case (p. 30) were added.

items.name: Transfer factors on maximally split tori, and Lemma 3.6
items.statement: At a p-adic place, ∆_0 = ∆_I∆_II∆_III,1∆_III,2∆_IV with ∆_I = ∆_III,1 = 1 (H^1(F, T_sc) = 1), ∆_II = 1 for trivial χ-data (allowed because the maximally split torus has no symmetric roots; the a-data satisfy a_{−α} = −a_α), ∆_IV = D_G(t)/D_H(t_H); and (Lemma 3.6) for associated t ∈ T_G and t_H = (t_0, z_1, z_2) ∈ T_H ⊂ U(m) × U(4), ∆(t_H, t) = μ(z_1)μ(z_2)∆_IV(t_H, t). At archimedean places Kottwitz's factor equals ±∆_0, the sign cancelling when [F:Q] is even.
items.note: Langlands–Shelstad transfer factors are planned in EndoscopicTransfer ET.1; the explicit computation for this embedding ξ is not. Review (REV-PAPER-CLOZEL-THORNE-17): ∆_II was corrected; at finite places the Whittaker-normalised factors equal the Langlands–Shelstad ∆₀ (asserted via [CT15, §3.5]). The review checked a(σ) = diag(1, 1, 1_m, −1, −1) from (3.1).

items.name: Proposition 3.7 (Mœglin): a Jacquet module exponent of the endoscopic packet
items.statement: For m = 5 (n = 9), let H = U(1) × U(8) be the endoscopic group of type (1, n − 1) attached to ε₁, with the embedding ξ sending w ∈ W_E to diag(1, μ(w)1_{n−1}), and let π₁, π₂ be the two-element (unstable) L-packet of U(8) attached to μ^{−1}(sp(3) ⊕ sp(5)). Then the Jacquet module of π_H = 1 ⊗ (π₁ ⊕ π₂) contains the character μ(z)^{−1}[2, 1, 0, −1] of T_H with multiplicity 2, and the identity Σ_π ε₁(π)⟨tr π, f⟩ = ⟨tr π_H, f^H⟩ holds. More generally, for n = a + b with a ≤ b odd and π the L-packet attached to St_{a,E} ⊞ St_{b,E}, the full Jacquet module contains [(b − 1)/2, (b − 3)/2, …, (1 − a)/2] (the μ-twist neglected).
items.note: Proved by Mœglin's hereditary formula for Jacquet modules, as in [CT15, Appendix A]. Review (REV-PAPER-CLOZEL-THORNE-17): material correction: π_H here is the packet of the (1, n − 1) endoscopic datum defined on p. 27 for this purpose, not the packet St_m ⊗ π_4^± of (3.7), whose Jacquet module does not contain [2, 1, 0, −1]. The proposition is used only to fix the labels ε₁ (p. 27: 'this is not necessary for the proof of our main results, only ε = ε₁ε₂ being relevant'). Its proof uses Mœglin's hereditary formula Jac_{|·|²}(St₅ ⊞ St₃) = St₃ ⊞ St₃.

items.name: Theorem 3.8(1): automorphic representations of the definite unitary group with endoscopic base change
items.statement: Let G be the unitary group in n = l + 2 variables over F (l > 5 prime), split by the CM field E, compact at infinity and quasi-split at finite places, [F:Q] even. Let σ_1, σ_2 be conjugate self-dual cuspidal representations of GL_4(A_E), GL_m(A_E) with (a) σ_1 ⊞ σ_2 regular algebraic of infinity type ((l + 1)/2, (l − 1)/2, …, (−1 − l)/2) at every infinite place and ∏_{v|∞} det(w_v) = 1; (b) places v_0, …, v_s ramified in E of odd residue characteristic with σ_{1,w_i} ≅ St_3 ⊞ St_1, σ_{2,w_i} ≅ St_m; (c) every other ramified place of σ_1 ⊞ σ_2 split over F, and no other place of F ramified in E. Then there are exactly 4^{s+1}/2 automorphic representations σ of G(A_F) with stable base change σ_1 ⊞ σ_2, each of multiplicity one, in bijection with the tuples (σ_{v_i}) ∈ ∏ Π_{φ_{v_i}} with ∏ ε_{v_i}(σ_{v_i}) = 1.
items.locator: Theorem 3.8, accepted manuscript p. 28; part 1; Remark 3.9, p. 29
items.note: Remark 3.9: ∏ det(w_v) = 1 holds if every place above l splits in E with [F_v : Q_l] even and σ_1 ⊞ σ_2 is ι-ordinary ([CT14, Lemma 2.6]); equivalently a Shelstad sign.

items.name: Theorem 3.8(2): the same count for a cuspidal base change, and strong stable base change for G
items.statement: Let π be a RACSDC representation of GL_n(A_E) regular algebraic of the same infinity type with π_{w_i} ≅ St_m ⊞ St_3 ⊞ St_1 at places v_0, …, v_s as in Theorem 3.8(1) and the same splitting conditions. Then there are exactly 4^{s+1} automorphic representations of G(A_F) with stable base change π, each of multiplicity one, in bijection with ∏ Π_{φ_{v_i}}. (Remark after the proof, pp. 30–31: an automorphic σ of G(A_F) with σ_∞ trivial whose Galois representation is irreducible or has constituents of dimensions (4, m) has a strong stable base change to GL_n(A_E), well defined when its local components are tempered, with π cohomological of trivial infinitesimal character.)
items.locator: Theorem 3.8, accepted manuscript pp. 28–29; part 2 and pp. 30–31
items.note: Review (REV-PAPER-CLOZEL-THORNE-17): the strong base change is a remark after the proof, for σ_∞ trivial, not part of Theorem 3.8; locator extended.

items.name: Theorem 3.10: the case l = 5 (n = 7)
items.statement: For n = 7, with σ_1, σ_2 of GL_4, GL_3 (σ_{2,w_i} ≅ St_3), the same hypotheses and the two-element packets {X_v, Y_v} (ε(X_v) = −1, ε(Y_v) = 1): there are exactly 2^s automorphic representations of G(A_F) with stable base change σ_1 ⊞ σ_2, in bijection with the tuples with ∏ ε = 1; and exactly 2^{s+1} with a cuspidal base change π with π_{w_i} ≅ St_3 ⊞ St_3 ⊞ St_1; stable base change holds.
items.note: Review (REV-PAPER-CLOZEL-THORNE-17): locator: the statement runs over pp. 31–32.

items.name: The level-raising set-up of §4.1: fields, places, the definite unitary group and the endoscopic datum
items.statement: Let l ≥ 5 be prime, ι: Q̄_l ≅ C, E a CM field with maximal totally real subfield F such that every place v | l of F splits in E with [F_v : Q_l] even, and places v_0, …, v_s (s ≥ 1) of F ramified in E of odd residue characteristic with q_{v_0} ≡ −1 mod l and each q_{v_i} (i ≥ 1) a primitive root mod l, every other place unramified in E. Let n = l + 2, m = l − 2 and G the unitary group in n variables split by E, compact at infinity and quasi-split at every finite place. Let π_1, π_2 be cuspidal conjugate self-dual representations of GL_m(A_E), GL_4(A_E) with π_{1,w_i} ≅ St_m, π_{2,w_i} ≅ St_3 ⊞ St_1, other ramification split over F; π = π_1 ⊞ π_2 regular algebraic, ι-ordinary of infinity type ((n − 1)/2, …, (1 − n)/2); r̄_ι(π) = ρ̄_1 ⊕ ρ̄_2 with ρ̄_i absolutely irreducible of dimensions m and 4; ρ̄_1(t_{w_i}) regular unipotent and ρ̄_2(t_{w_i}) of Jordan type 3 + 1 for a generator t_{w_i} of tame inertia.

items.name: Algebraic modular forms S(U, A) on the definite unitary group, their Hecke algebras T(U, O), ordinary parts and the maximal ideals m, m^∨
items.statement: For an open compact U ⊂ G(A_F^∞) and an O-algebra A, S(U, A) is the space of functions G(F)\G(A_F^∞)/U → A (weight zero). With the integral model, identifications ι_w: G(F_v) ≅ GL_n(E_w) at split places and uniformisers at places above l of [CT15, §3.3], the Hecke algebra T(U, O) ⊂ End_O(S(U, O)) is generated by the unramified operators at split places of maximal level and the operators U_v^j at v | l. An automorphic Σ with trivial Σ_∞ contributes to N ⊂ S(U, O) if N ∩ ι^{−1}Σ^{∞,U,ord} ≠ 0. Levels: U_{0,v_0} = P_{v_0}, U_{0,v_i} = B_{v_i} (i ≥ 1), hyperspecial at inert places, Iw(c) at places above l, U_0 sufficiently small with σ^{U_0} ≠ 0; U_1 equals U_0 except U_{1,v_0} = B_{v_0}, so [U_0 : U_1] = q_{v_0} + 1. m ⊂ T(U_1, O) is the maximal ideal of σ and m^∨ that of σ^∨.
items.note: AutomorphicFormsOnReductiveGroups AF.5 plans the identification of algebraic modular forms on compact-at-infinity groups with functions on finite adelic double cosets; the Hecke algebras and ordinary parts on definite unitary groups are in the Part II PolarizedAutomorphyLifting proposed by the Boxer–Calegari–Gee extraction (not yet in the atlas).

items.name: Proposition 4.1: the local types of automorphic representations contributing to S(U_1, O)_m
items.statement: If Σ contributes to S(U_1, O)_m and Π is its stable base change to GL_n(A_E) (a RACSD representation), then Π is ι-ordinary and either (1) Π_{w_i} ≅ St_m ⊞ St_3 ⊞ St_1 for every i = 0, …, s, or (2) for some i, r_ι(Π)(t_{w_i}) has Jordan decomposition of partition n = (n − 2) + 1 + 1 or n = n, and Π is cuspidal.
items.note: The proof corrects the proof of [CT15, Lemma 4.3] (semistability of Π_w) and uses the closure order on nilpotent classes (dim ker N^j ≤ dim ker N̄^j), the parity condition of Mok's Lemma 2.2.1, and quadratic characters ≡ 1 mod λ. Review (REV-PAPER-CLOZEL-THORNE-17): locator: the two cases are printed on p. 35.

items.name: Proposition 4.3: the perfect pairing on S(U_1) and its vanishing on S(U_0) mod l
items.statement: The pairing ⟨f, g⟩ = Σ_{x ∈ G(F)\G(A^∞_F)/U_1} f(x)g(x) on S(U_1, O) satisfies ⟨af, g⟩ = ⟨f, ȷ(a)g⟩ for a ∈ H_{B_{v_0},O} and induces (1) perfect pairings S(U_1, O)_m × S(U_1, O)_{m^∨} → O and S(U_1, k)_m × S(U_1, k)_{m^∨} → k; (2) a pairing vanishing on S(U_0, k)_m × S(U_0, k)_{m^∨} (because q_{v_0} ≡ −1 mod l); (3) a perfect pairing M × N → O whose reduction vanishes on M^{U_0} ⊗ k × N^{U_0} ⊗ k, for the isotypic submodule M of the proof of Theorem 4.2 (the intersection of the R_i^{B_{v_i}}-isotypic parts of S(U_1, O)_m) and the analogous submodule N of S(U_1, O)_{m^∨}.
items.locator: Proposition 4.3, accepted manuscript p. 36; as in [CT15, Proposition 4.5]
items.note: Review (REV-PAPER-CLOZEL-THORNE-17): ȷ is the canonical anti-involution; the paper uses N without defining it (sourceIssues E14), and the intended definition was supplied.

items.name: Lemma 4.4: the structure of M as an H_{B_{v_0}}-module
items.statement: Under the hypothesis (⋆) of the proof of Theorem 4.2, M ⊗_{O,ι} C ≅ (X^{B_{v_0}}_{v_0})^a ⊕ (Y^{B_{v_0}}_{v_0})^b ⊕ (Z^{B_{v_0}}_{v_0})^c ≅ N ⊗_{O,ι} C as H_{B_{v_0},C}-modules, with a > b = c ≥ 0.
items.note: Endoscopic (non-cuspidal) base changes contribute only X at v_0, cuspidal ones X, Y and Z; the endoscopic set is non-empty because of the initial datum π_1 ⊞ π_2.

items.name: Theorem 4.2: level-raising for l = 5 and l = 7
items.statement: In the set-up of §4.1 with l = 5 or l = 7, there is an automorphic representation Σ of G(A_F) contributing to S(U_1, O)_m that falls into case 2 of Proposition 4.1: its base change is cuspidal and at some w_i the monodromy has Jordan type (n − 2) + 1 + 1 or n.
items.locator: Theorem 4.2, accepted manuscript p. 35; proof pp. 35–37; Remark 4.5
items.note: Proof by contradiction: choosing R_i with ∏ ε_{v_i}(R_i) = −1 (i ≥ 1), the P_{v_0}-fixed part M_1 of M(χ̄) has rank a + b (Proposition 2.9) and is isotropic mod l, while M(χ̄) has rank a + 3b (X has one exponent ≡ [2, 1, 0, −1], Y three, Z none, as q_{v_0} ≡ −1 mod l); so 2(a + b) ≤ a + 3b, contradicting a > b. Remark 4.5: the count fails for l > 7 since Z(χ̄) ≠ 0.

items.name: Local deformation problems at places of L^+: ordinary, unrestricted, R^χ_v, R^St_v, and the new partition rings R^m_v
items.statement: For v ∈ T_L: R^Δ_v the ordinary lifting ring (v | l; Geraghty, [Tho15, §3.3.2]); R^□_v the unrestricted ring (v ∈ S_{a,L}, formally smooth, unramified universal lift); for v ∤ l with q_v ≡ 1 mod l and characters χ_{v,i}: O^×_{L_ṽ} → O^× trivial mod λ, R^{χ_v}_v classifying lifts whose inertia has characteristic polynomial ∏(X − χ_{v,i}) (R^1_v when all are trivial); R^St_v classifying unipotently ramified lifts with Frobenius eigenvalues α, q_vα, …, q_v^{n−1}α; and, for a partition m = (m_1 ≥ ⋯ ≥ m_k) of n, R^m_v, the maximal O-flat reduced quotient of R^1_v classifying lifts for which a lift of Frob_ṽ^{−1} has characteristic polynomial in Taylor's scheme Pol_n(m, q_v) (so R^{(n)}_v = R^St_v).
items.note: The first four are planned in LocalGaloisDeformationRings L7 ('semistable, Steinberg and minimally ramified analogues away from p for rank n') and R08.2; R^m_v is new here. A local deformation problem is determined by its ring (Barnet-Lamb–Geraghty–Harris–Taylor, Lemma 3.2). Review (REV-PAPER-CLOZEL-THORNE-17): the unrestricted ring is R^□_v; R_v denotes the chosen ring at v ∈ R.

items.name: Lemma 5.2: R^1_v[1/l] is smooth at pure points of R^m_v, with a unique minimal prime there
items.statement: Let x ∈ Spec R^m_v[1/l] be a closed point given by ρ: G_{L_ṽ} → GL_n(O) with ρ ⊗ Q̄_l pure (Taylor–Yoshida, Lemma 1.4). Then Spec R^1_v[1/l] is formally smooth over K at x, there is a unique minimal prime Q_v of R^1_v in the kernel of R^1_v → O, and Q_v contains ker(R^1_v → R^m_v).
items.note: Uses that (R^1_v)^red is O-flat equidimensional of dimension 1 + n² (Taylor 2008, Proposition 3.1; Thorne 2012, Lemma 3.15) and that Spec R_v[1/l] is equidimensional of dimension n² and smooth at pure points (BLGGT14, Lemma 1.3.2).

items.name: Deformation data D = (L, {R_v}) and the attached objects of [Tho15]: Λ_L, S({R_v}), U, S_D, T_D, R_D, P_D, J_D, R^red_D
items.statement: For a good soluble CM extension L/E (every place of V_0 ∪ S_a split), a set R of places of L^+ above T ∖ (S_l ∪ S_a) and local rings R_v of types 3–5: the Iwasawa algebra Λ_L = ⊗̂_{v∈S_{l,L}} O⟦(I_{L_ṽ}(l)^{ab})^n⟧; the global deformation problem S({R_v}) of type (L/L^+, R ∪ S_{l,L} ∪ S_{a,L}, …, Λ_L, r̄, ε^{1−n}δ^n_{L/L^+}, {R^Δ_v}_{v∈S_{l,L}} ∪ {R^□_v}_{v∈S_{a,L}} ∪ {R_v}_{v∈R}); the level U; the space of modular forms S_D = S_χ(U(l^∞), K/O)^∨, finite free over Λ_L; the Hecke algebra T_D localised at the maximal ideal of a descent to G of the everywhere unramified auxiliary Π′ of the preliminary reductions (item 073); the universal deformation ring R_D ⊃ the universal pseudodeformation ring P_D (finite); a surjection P_D → T_D with kernel I_D and J_D = I_D R_D when every R_v (v ∈ R ∖ (S_{l,L} ∪ S_{a,L})) is some R^{χ_v}_v, including R^1_v; and the reducible quotient R^red_D. T_D is finite torsion-free over Λ_L, and when every R_v is R^{χ_v}_v or R^St_v each minimal prime of R_D has dimension ≥ 1 + n[L^+ : Q].
items.note: From Thorne, Automorphy lifting for residually reducible l-adic Galois representations (JAMS 2015), Propositions 3.8, 3.9, 3.29, 4.3, Definitions 3.27, 3.31, 4.2; the group 𝒢_n of Clozel–Harris–Taylor §2.1. A prerequisite paper; not planned in the atlas (GlobalGaloisDeformations G7 plans polarized deformation problems, but not pseudodeformations of reducible r̄). Review (REV-PAPER-CLOZEL-THORNE-17): three fixes against p. 40 (Π′, not Π_0; the unrestricted rings at S_{a,L}; the condition for P_D → T_D). The objects Λ_L, S({R_v}), S_D, T_D, R_D, P_D, J_D, R^red_D are Thorne 2015's, imported from PolarizedAutomorphyLifting (route 5); the deformation datum packaging is this paper's.

items.name: Thorne's R = T and automorphy lifting for residually reducible representations (inputs from [Tho15])
items.statement: (1) [Tho15, Theorem 4.19, Corollary 4.20]: under hypotheses (1)–(5) there, for a minimal prime Q_1 ⊂ R_{D_1} inside a suitable prime, J_{D_1} ⊂ Q_1 and R_{D_1}/Q_1 is finite over Λ_L of dimension dim Λ_L. (2) [Tho15, Theorem 7.1]: automorphy lifting for ρ̄ = ρ̄_1 ⊕ ρ̄_2 Schur, ordinary, given an automorphic ordinary lift that is Steinberg at some place. (3) [Tho15, Lemmas 1.9, 3.36, Corollary 4.14, Proposition 4.18]: dimension-one primes avoiding countably many small quotients, twisting by ∆/(c + 1), and soluble base change of Hecke algebras. (4) Hida classicality for GL_n over CM fields (Geraghty, Lemma 2.6.4) and the identification of the modules S/λ as χ varies (Geraghty, Lemma 2.2.6). (5) [Tho15, Corollary 5.7] with the conditions at the start of [Tho15, §5.2] (giving hypothesis (1) of [Tho15, Theorem 4.19]) and [Tho15, Proposition 4.12] (the surjection P_D → T_D).
items.locator: Proofs of Lemmas 5.3–5.6, Theorems 5.1 and 5.7, accepted manuscript pp. 40–44
items.note: Stated inputs from Thorne 2015 and Geraghty's preprint; prerequisites. The Boxer–Calegari–Gee extraction's proposed Part II PolarizedAutomorphyLifting plans Thorne 2012/2017 and BLGGT14 but not Thorne 2015. Review (REV-PAPER-CLOZEL-THORNE-17): the further Thorne 2015 and Geraghty inputs used on pp. 40–43 were added. Rerouted to PolarizedAutomorphyLifting (route 5), which owns the residually reducible theory of Thorne 2015 and Allen–Newton–Thorne 2020 in the reviews of the Newton–Thorne extractions.

items.name: Lemma 5.3: dimension of the reducible locus with Steinberg-type conditions
items.statement: Fix a partition m with m_1 > n_1 = dim ρ̄_1 and a deformation datum D = (L, {R_v}_{v∈R_0} ∪ {R^m_v}_{v∈R_1}). Let ∆ (resp. ∆') be the Galois group of the maximal abelian l-extension of L unramified outside l (resp. in addition split at R̃_1 ∪ R̃^c_1) and d = dim_{Q_l} ker(∆ ⊗ Q_l → ∆' ⊗ Q_l)^{c=−1}. Then dim R^red_D ≤ 1 + n[L^+ : Q] − d and R^red_D is finite over Λ_L.
items.note: The key point: a reducible deformation (r̄_1 ⊗ Ψ_1) ⊕ (r̄_2 ⊗ Ψ_2) of type R^m_v forces Ψ_1(Frob_ṽ) = Ψ_2(Frob_ṽ), since m_1 > n_1 > n_2. Uses the potential ordinary automorphy of ρ̄_1, ρ̄_2 (hypothesis 4 of Theorem 5.1). Review (REV-PAPER-CLOZEL-THORNE-17): the proof imposes R^1_v at R₀ in the auxiliary problems S₁, S₂, so it covers only R_v of unipotent type at R₀; the only application has R₀ = ∅ (sourceIssues E21). The printed step 'an eigenvalue of multiplicity m₁ … modulo the nilradical of J' should read 'multiplicity at least m₁ … Ψ₁(Frob_ṽ) − Ψ₂(Frob_ṽ) ∈ √J' (E17).

items.name: Lemma 5.4: dim R_D/J_{D'}R_D = dim Λ_L for the partition of the monodromy at w_0
items.statement: Let D = (L, {R^{χ_v}_v}_{v∈R_0} ∪ {R^m_v}_{v∈R_1}) with m the Jordan type of N, rec^T(Π_{w_0}) = (r, N), R_1 the places above v_0, and D' = (L, {R^{χ_v}_v}_{v∈R_0} ∪ {R^1_v}_{v∈R_1}). Then dim R_D/J_{D'}R_D = dim Λ_L.

items.name: Lemma 5.5: changing the characters χ_v after a soluble base change
items.statement: Let D_0^χ = (L_0, {R^{χ_v}_v}_{v∈R}) with pairwise distinct χ_{v,1}, …, χ_{v,n} for each v ∈ R, and L ⊃ L_0 good with every χ_{v,i} trivial on inertia of L above R. For D = (L, ∅) there is a commutative diagram R_D ← P_D → T_D over R^nil_{D_0^χ} ← P^nil_{D_0^χ} → T_{D_0^χ}.
items.note: Uses soluble base change and descent for G ([CT14, Proposition 2.9]); this is why n_1 ≠ n_2 and n_1n_2 even are assumed. Review (REV-PAPER-CLOZEL-THORNE-17): locator: the statement continues onto p. 42.

items.name: Lemma 5.6: a characteristic-l prime of R_D containing J_D yields a Steinberg automorphic lift
items.statement: Suppose a deformation datum D = (L, ∅) and a dimension-one prime 𝔭 ⊂ R_D of characteristic l satisfy: (1) r_𝔭: G_L → GL_n(Frac A) is absolutely irreducible (A the normalisation of R_D/𝔭); (2) the characters ψ^v_1, …, ψ^v_n of I_{L_ṽ} (v ∈ S_{l,L}) are pairwise distinct; (3) for some v ∈ S_{l,L} some σ ∈ I_{L_ṽ} has r_𝔭(σ) with eigenvalues satisfying no non-trivial Z-linear relation; (4) J_D ⊂ 𝔭; (5) r_𝔭|_{G_{L_ũ}} is trivial for some u ∈ T_L ∖ (S_{l,L} ∪ S_{a,L}). Then there is an ι-ordinary RACSDC Π_1 of GL_n(A_L) with r̄_ι(Π_1) ≅ r̄_ι(Π)|_{G_L} and Π_{1,ũ} an unramified twist of Steinberg.
items.note: Review (REV-PAPER-CLOZEL-THORNE-17): condition (3) corrected against p. 42: the place v ∈ S_{l,L} and r_𝔭(σ) were missing.

items.name: Theorem 5.1: level-raising to Steinberg for residually reducible representations
items.statement: Let E be imaginary CM, n ≥ 2, Π a RACSDC representation of GL_n(A_E) with r̄_ι(Π) = ρ̄_1 ⊕ ρ̄_2, ρ̄_i absolutely irreducible, non-isomorphic, ρ̄_i^c ≅ ρ̄_i^∨ ε^{1−n}, n_1 > n_2, r̄_ι(Π) primitive, and a place w_0 where Π_{w_0} is Iwahori-spherical and N in rec^T(Π_{w_0}) = (r, N) has a Jordan block of length > n_1. Assume (1) Π is ι-ordinary; (2) l > 3, l ∤ n_1, n_2, n, and n_1n_2 even; (3) each ρ̄_i|_{G_{E(ζ_l)}} is adequate and E(ζ_l) ⊄ the fixed field of ad r̄_ι(Π); (4) a CM E_0/E linearly disjoint from the extension of E(ζ_l) cut out by r̄_ι(Π) and ι-ordinary RAECSDC (π_i, χ_i) of GL_{n_i}(A_{E_0}) with r̄_ι(π_i) ≅ ρ̄_i|_{G_{E_0}}. Then there are a soluble CM E_1/E linearly disjoint from the extension of E(ζ_l) cut out by r̄_ι(Π) and an ι-ordinary RACSDC Π_1 of GL_n(A_{E_1}) with r̄_ι(Π_1) ≅ r̄_ι(Π)|_{G_{E_1}} and Π_{1,w_1} an unramified twist of Steinberg at a place w_1 | w_0.
items.locator: Theorem 5.1, accepted manuscript pp. 37–38; proof pp. 38–43
items.note: Review (REV-PAPER-CLOZEL-THORNE-17): hypothesis (4) and the standing assumptions were corrected against pp. 37–38. The proof asserts that r_{𝔭₀} is primitive, which is not shown; irreducibility of r_𝔭 follows instead from Clifford theory and n₁ ≠ n₂ (sourceIssues E20).

items.name: Theorem 5.7: automorphy lifting for residually reducible ρ from a lift with a large Jordan block
items.statement: Let E be CM and ρ: G_E → GL_n(Q̄_l) continuous with (1) ρ^c ≅ ρ^∨ε^{1−n}; (2) finitely many ramified places; (3) ρ ordinary of weight λ ([Tho15, Definition 2.5]); (4) l > 3 and E(ζ_l) ⊄ the field cut out by ad ρ̄; (5) ρ̄ ≅ ρ̄_1 ⊕ ρ̄_2 with ρ̄_i|_{G_{E(ζ_l)}} adequate, n_1 ≠ n_2, n_1n_2 even, l ∤ n_1n_2(n_1 + n_2), ρ̄ primitive; (6) a place w_0 ∤ l with ρ|^ss_{G_{E_{w_0}}} ≅ ⊕_{i=1}^n ψε^{n−i}, ψ unramified; (7) an ι-ordinary RACSDC Π with r̄_ι(Π) ≅ ρ̄ whose N at w_0 has a Jordan block of length > max(n_1, n_2); (8) as hypothesis 4 of Theorem 5.1. Then ρ ≅ r_ι(π) for a RACSDC automorphic representation π of GL_n(A_E).
items.note: Combines Theorem 5.1 with [Tho15, Theorem 7.1] and soluble descent; the paper states it 'to streamline its later application' in §6.

items.name: The congruence Sym^{l+1} r̄ ≅ (φr̄ ⊗ r̄) ⊕ χ² Sym^{l−3} r̄ for two-dimensional mod l representations
items.statement: For a two-dimensional representation r̄ with values in GL_2(F̄_l), determinant χ, and φ the (arithmetic) Frobenius acting on coefficients, (Sym^{l+1} r̄)^ss ≅ (φr̄ ⊗ r̄) ⊕ χ² Sym^{l−3} r̄: Sym^{l+1} of the standard representation of GL₂ has the two composition factors L(l+1) = V ⊗ V^{(1)} (Steinberg's tensor product theorem, dimension 4) and det² ⊗ Sym^{l−3}V (dimension l − 2). If the image of r̄ contains SL₂(F_{l^a}) with a > 1, both summands are irreducible; for a = 1, φr̄ ≅ r̄ and φr̄ ⊗ r̄ contains det.
items.locator: (1.1), accepted manuscript p. 2 (l = 7); proof of Theorem 6.2, p. 45 (general l)
items.note: Review (REV-PAPER-CLOZEL-THORNE-17): (1.1) is printed on p. 2 only for l = 7 ('Sym⁸ r̄ ∼ (φr̄ ⊗ r̄) ⊕ χ² Sym⁴ r̄'); the general form is in the proof of Theorem 6.2 (p. 45). 'Large image' was made precise and the decomposition checked by linkage. Rerouted to ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations G7 (route 7): it is the r = 2 case of the identity (1.1) of PAPER-NEWTON-THORNE-26 (residual-symmetric-power-decomposition), which is routed there.

items.name: Known functorial transfers used: Gelbart–Jacquet, Kim–Shahidi, Kim, Ramakrishnan and Arthur–Clozel
items.statement: (1) Sym² π exists for cuspidal π of GL_2(A_F) and is cuspidal iff π is not automorphically induced from a quadratic extension iff π ≇ π ⊗ η for all non-trivial Hecke characters η (Gelbart–Jacquet; Theorem 7.3(1)); if Sym² π is cuspidal, π_E and Sym² π_E stay cuspidal after any quadratic base change (Arthur–Clozel, Theorem 3.4.2; Theorem 7.3(2)). (2) Sym³ π (Kim–Shahidi) and Sym⁴ π (Kim) exist. (3) Ramakrishnan's Theorem M: the Rankin–Selberg product of two cuspidal representations of GL_2 is automorphic on GL_4.
items.locator: Theorem 7.3, accepted manuscript p. 47; proof of Theorem 6.2, p. 46; Corollary 7.2(1)
items.note: ML.5 plans to 'register cyclic base change, automorphic induction and selected tensor/symmetric-power transfers with exact hypotheses'.

items.name: Change of weight and base-change inputs from [CT14], [CT15] and [CHT08]
items.statement: [CT15, Proposition 3.10] with base change for U_2: a RACSDC π′_2 of GL_2(A_{E_2}), ι-ordinary with HT_τ = {(1 − l)/2, (1 + l)/2}, with π′_{2,z} ≅ St_2 ⊗ ιω at the places z above u_0 (ω the Teichmüller lift of ε̄^{(l−1)/2}), r̄_ι(π′_2) ≅ ε̄^{(l−1)/2} ⊗ ρ̄_2, and such that if π′_2 is ramified at a place w ∤ u_0 of E_2 then w is split over F_2.
items.locator: Proof of Theorem 6.2, accepted manuscript pp. 45–46
items.note: Stated inputs from the earlier papers of the series (Compositio 2014, Annals 2015) and Clozel–Harris–Taylor; prerequisites. The proof of Theorem 6.1 also follows 'a series of reductions … essentially the same as those of [CT15, §6]'. Review (REV-PAPER-CLOZEL-THORNE-17): material correction: the item said π′_2 is 'ramified only above split places', but it is Steinberg (ramified) at the places above u_0, which are ramified in E_2/F_2 (p. 46). The item was split: [CT14, Lemma 2.6] and [CT14, Proposition 2.9] are now item 059 (route 5), and [CHT08, Lemma 4.1.4] item 060 (route 8), each with the owner the Newton–Thorne extractions give it.

items.name: Theorem 6.2: Sym^{l+1} ρ is automorphic for l ∈ {5, 7} under ordinarity and Steinberg hypotheses
items.statement: Let l ∈ {5, 7}, F totally real, ι: Q̄_l ≅ C, and (π, χ) a RAESDC representation of GL_2(A_F) with (1) π ι-ordinary of weight zero (infinity type (1/2, −1/2) at every real place); (2) ρ̄ = r̄_ι(π) irreducible with image containing a conjugate of SL_2(F_{l^a}) for some a > 1, and (φρ̄ ⊗ ρ̄)|_{G_{F(ζ_l)}} and (Sym^{l−3} ρ̄)|_{G_{F(ζ_l)}} adequate; (3) a place u_0 ∤ 2 with π_{u_0} an unramified twist of Steinberg, q_{u_0} a primitive root mod l and ρ̄ ramified at u_0. Then Sym^{l+1} ρ is automorphic.
items.note: Proof: pass to a CM field E_2 with places above u_0 ramified in E_2/F_2 (q ≡ −1 at one, primitive roots at the others), build Π_1 ⊞ Π_2 of type (4, l − 2) with the congruence of item 046, apply Theorem 4.2 and then Theorem 5.7, and descend. Corrected for source issue E4 (E_2 = F_2·E_1). Review (REV-PAPER-CLOZEL-THORNE-17): the printed proof does not verify hypothesis (4) of Theorem 5.7 (E_0(ζ_l) not contained in the field cut out by ad ρ̄); by Dickson it can fail only if [F(ζ_l) : F] = 2 and the quadratic subfield of F(proj ρ̄) is F(ζ_l), which Theorem 6.2's hypotheses do not exclude (sourceIssues E22). Theorem 6.1's hypothesis F ∩ Q(ζ_l) = Q excludes it.

items.name: Theorem 6.1 (Theorem 1.1): the 6th and 8th symmetric powers
items.statement: Let F be totally real and (π, χ) a RAESDC representation of GL_2(A_F) not automorphically induced from a quadratic CM extension. (1) If F ∩ Q(ζ_5) = Q, the 6th symmetric power lift of π exists as a cuspidal automorphic representation of GL_7(A_F). (2) If F ∩ Q(ζ_7) = Q, the 8th symmetric power lift exists as a cuspidal automorphic representation of GL_9(A_F).
items.locator: Theorem 6.1, accepted manuscript p. 44; Theorem 1.1, p. 2
items.note: Deduced from Theorem 6.2 by the reductions of [CT15, §6]. Superseded in range, by a different method, by Newton–Thorne (PAPER-NEWTON-THORNE-21, -21-B, -26); ML.3 should keep the hypotheses of each source.

items.name: Theorem 7.1: reduction of the mixed-parity case to the RAESDC case
items.statement: Let F be totally real and r ≥ 1. Suppose that for every RAESDC (π, χ) of GL_2(A_F) not automorphically induced from a quadratic CM extension there is a RAESDC (Π, Ξ) of GL_{r+1}(A_F) with Sym^r rec_{F_v}(π_v) ≅ rec_{F_v}(Π_v) at all finite v. Then for every cuspidal π of GL_2(A_F) with π_∞ essentially square-integrable and not automorphically induced from a quadratic CM extension there is a cuspidal Π of GL_{r+1}(A_F) with Sym^r rec_{F_v}(π_v) ≅ rec_{F_v}(Π_v) at all finite v; in particular L(Sym^r π, s) = L(Π, s) continues to an entire function with the expected functional equation.
items.note: Mixed-parity π become algebraic up to twist after base change to a CM field (Blasius–Rogawski). Review (REV-PAPER-CLOZEL-THORNE-17): for π_∞ essentially square-integrable, 'not induced from a quadratic CM extension' is equivalent to Sym²π cuspidal (item 081), which the proof uses silently. The descent in the proof is determined only up to η_{E/F} (sourceIssues E23).

items.name: Corollary 7.2 (with Corollaries 1.2 and 1.3): symmetric powers up to 8
items.statement: Let F be totally real and π cuspidal on GL_2(A_F) with π_∞ essentially square-integrable, not automorphically induced from a quadratic CM extension. There is a cuspidal Π of GL_{r+1}(A_F) with Sym^r rec_{F_v}(π_v) ≅ rec_{F_v}(Π_v) at all finite v in each case: (1) F arbitrary, 1 ≤ r ≤ 4; (2) F ∩ Q(ζ_5) = Q, r ∈ {5, 6}; (3) F ∩ Q(ζ_35) = Q, r = 7; (4) F ∩ Q(ζ_7) = Q, r = 8. Hence L(Sym^r π, s) is entire with the expected functional equation (Corollary 1.3).
items.locator: Corollary 7.2, accepted manuscript pp. 46–47; Corollaries 1.2–1.3, p. 2
items.note: Cases r = 5, 7 are [CT15, Theorem 1.2]; r ≤ 4 are Gelbart–Jacquet, Kim–Shahidi and Kim. Review (REV-PAPER-CLOZEL-THORNE-17): locator: the statement spans pp. 46–47.

items.name: Lemma 7.4: twisting π_E to a RACSDC representation
items.statement: Let F be totally real, π cuspidal on GL_2(A_F) with π_∞ essentially square-integrable, and E/F an imaginary CM extension with π_E cuspidal. Then there is a continuous character χ: E^×\A_E^× → C^× with π_E ⊗ χ RACSDC.
items.note: Uses Chevalley's congruence subgroup theorem for units (to make the central character finite order) and [CHT08, Lemma 4.1.4].

items.name: Lemma 7.5: large residual image for a density-one set of primes
items.statement: Let E be imaginary CM and π a RACSDC representation of GL_2(A_E) with Sym² π cuspidal. Then there is a set L of rational primes of Dirichlet density 1 such that for all l ∈ L and all ι: Q̄_l ≅ C, r̄_ι(π) is irreducible with image containing a conjugate of SL_2(F_l).
items.note: Uses BLGGT14 Theorem 5.5.2 and Proposition 5.3.2, Fontaine–Laffaille's description of r̄_ι(π)|_{I_v} for l large (so that α_2/α_1 has order > 5), and the classification of finite subgroups of PGL_2(F̄_l).

items.name: Potential diagonalisability and automorphy inputs from Barnet-Lamb–Gee–Geraghty–Taylor
items.statement: [BLGGT14, Theorem 4.4.1] and 'a standard extension of this result to a totally real base field': an odd irreducible R̄ : G_F → GL_2(F̄_l) with suitable large image has a potentially diagonalisable lift, unramified almost everywhere; [BLGGT14, Theorem 5.5.2, Proposition 5.3.2]: irreducibility of r_ι(π) and Sym² r_ι(π) and of their reductions for a density-one set of l.
items.locator: Proofs of Lemma 7.5 and Proposition 7.6, accepted manuscript pp. 48–49
items.note: ModularityAndLanglandsExtensions ML.2 assembles potential automorphy from these theorems; the Boxer–Calegari–Gee extraction's proposed PolarizedAutomorphyLifting plans other parts of BLGGT14 (§2 and Appendix A). Review (REV-PAPER-CLOZEL-THORNE-17): the item was split: BLGGT14 Theorem 4.2.1 and Lemma 1.4.3 (used for both R|G_E and, by Fontaine–Laffaille, for r_ι(Π)) are now item 058, routed to PolarizedAutomorphyLifting as in the Newton–Thorne extractions.

items.name: Proposition 7.6: symmetric powers over a CM field from those over its totally real subfield
items.statement: Let E/F be an imaginary CM quadratic extension and r ≥ 1. If Sym^r r_ι(π) is automorphic for every RAESDC (π, χ) of GL_2(A_F) not automorphically induced from a CM extension, then Sym^r r_ι(Π) is automorphic for every RACSDC Π of GL_2(A_E) not automorphically induced from a quadratic extension.
items.note: Proof: by Lemma 7.5 pick l > 2(r + 2) with large residual image; extend r̄_ι(Π) ⊗ φ to an odd R̄ of G_F; lift R̄ potentially diagonalisably (BLGGT14 Theorem 4.4.1); R is automorphic and Sym^r r_ι(Π) is residually potentially diagonalisably automorphic, hence automorphic (BLGGT14 Theorem 4.2.1). Corrected for source issue E5.

items.name: ι-ordinary automorphic representations
items.statement: For a RACSDC (or RAECSDC) Π of GL_n(A_E) of weight λ and ι : Q̄_l ≅ C, Π is ι-ordinary if at each v | l, Π_v is the generic subquotient of a normalized induction from smooth characters χ_{v,1}, …, χ_{v,n} with the valuations of ι^{−1}χ_{v,i}(ϖ_v) given by λ ([CT14, §2], after [Ger19]); then r_ι(Π) is ordinary of weight ιλ ([Tho15, Definition 2.5, Corollary 2.6]).
items.locator: §1.1, accepted manuscript p. 3 (conventions of [CT14, §2]); used throughout §§4–6
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-CLOZEL-THORNE-17. Split from item 002. As PAPER-NEWTON-THORNE-26 (iota-ordinary-automorphic), routed to PolarizedAutomorphyLifting.

items.name: BLGGT14 Theorem 4.2.1 and potential diagonalisability
items.statement: [BLGGT14, Theorem 4.2.1]: for F imaginary CM, l odd, (r, μ) regular algebraic, irreducible and polarized, potentially diagonalisable above l, with r̄|G_{F(ζ_l)} irreducible, l ≥ 2(d + 1), ζ_l ∉ F and (r̄, μ̄) ordinarily or potentially diagonalisably automorphic, (r, μ) is automorphic. [BLGGT14, Lemma 1.4.3]: potential diagonalisability is preserved by restriction, and Fontaine–Laffaille representations (l unramified, Hodge–Tate weights in an interval of length ≤ l − 2) are potentially diagonalisable.
items.locator: Proofs of Lemma 7.5 and Proposition 7.6, accepted manuscript pp. 48–49
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-CLOZEL-THORNE-17. Split from item 055; routed to PolarizedAutomorphyLifting, the owner of BLGGT14 Theorem 4.2.1 in the reviews of the three Newton–Thorne extractions.

items.name: Ordinarity of isobaric sums and base change for the definite unitary group ([CT14])
items.statement: [CT14, Lemma 2.6]: a regular algebraic isobaric sum of ι-ordinary conjugate self-dual cuspidal representations is ι-ordinary (with the signs det(w_v) of Remark 3.9). [CT14, Proposition 2.9]: soluble base change and descent between automorphic representations of the definite unitary group G and conjugate self-dual representations of GL_n.
items.locator: Proof of Theorem 6.2, p. 46; Remark 3.9, p. 29; Lemma 5.5, p. 42; §5.1, p. 40
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-CLOZEL-THORNE-17. Split from item 048. PolarizedAutomorphyLifting plans 'base change between GL_n over CM fields and definite unitary groups'; PAPER-NEWTON-THORNE-26 routes [CT14, Lemma 2.6] there.

items.name: [CHT08, Lemma 4.1.4]: algebraic Hecke characters with prescribed ψψ^c
items.statement: For a CM extension E/F and a character χ of type A₀ of F with the appropriate parity, there is a finite-order (or algebraic) character ψ of E, unramified at prescribed places, with ψψ^c = r_ι(χ)|G_E; hence a RAECSDC representation can be twisted to a RACSDC one.
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-CLOZEL-THORNE-17. Split from item 048. As PAPER-NEWTON-THORNE-26 (cht-twisting-lemma), routed to AutomorphicGaloisRepresentationsPartII AG2.2 ('For essentially conjugate self-dual forms, carry the algebraic twisting characters').

items.name: Borel–Casselman: Iwahori-spherical representations and Hecke modules
items.statement: For G = U_n, Sp_{2k} or PSp_{2k} over F and an Iwahori (or the parahoric B), V ↦ V^B is a bijection between irreducible admissible representations with V^B ≠ 0 and simple H_{B,C}-modules.
items.locator: Proof of Theorem 2.5, p. 10; proof of Proposition 2.6, p. 12
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-CLOZEL-THORNE-17. SR.1: 'prove smooth representations correspond to nondegenerate modules over the locally unital Hecke algebra, and identify e_U corners with U-biinvariant Hecke algebras'; the bijection on irreducibles with V^U ≠ 0 is its standard corollary.

items.name: Notation of §1.1
items.statement: Decomposition groups G_{F_v}, q_v, G_{F,S}, geometric Frobenius Frob_v, the semisimplified reduction ρ̄ of a continuous l-adic representation, normalised parabolic induction n-Ind, the normalised Jacquet module π^norm_N, and the Steinberg representations St_G and St_{n,F}.
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-CLOZEL-THORNE-17. SR.2 defines 'normalized induction/Jacquet functors using a specified square root of the modulus character'; R01.1–R01.2 the continuous representations, their reductions, decomposition groups and Frobenius.

items.name: Kazhdan–Lusztig standard modules: Jacquet modules and irreducibility
items.statement: For the triple (s, u, ρ) of Theorem 2.4, the semisimplified Jacquet module of the standard module is ⊕_α dim Hom_{M̄(u,s)}(ρ, H_*(B^α, C))·e^α over the M̄(u, s)-orbits B^α of components of B^s_u ([KL87, §7.6]), and in the tempered case the standard module is irreducible ([KL87, §8]).
items.locator: Proof of Theorem 2.5, accepted manuscript p. 11
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-CLOZEL-THORNE-17. Separated from item 013; routed with it.

items.name: The anti-involution ȷ, the Bernstein subalgebra O[Λ], localisations and the P-projector
items.statement: ȷ([BgB]) = [Bg^{−1}B] is the canonical anti-involution of H_{B,O}; O[Λ] ⊂ H_{B,O} is the abelian Bernstein subalgebra (requiring √q ∈ O and l ≠ p), with its image ȷO[Λ]; for an H_{B,O}-module M and a character χ̄ of O[Λ], M(χ̄) and M(χ̄ȷ) are the localisations at ker χ̄ and ker χ̄∘ȷ. e_P = [P]/(q + 1) = ([B] + [Bs_kB])/(q + 1) projects V^B onto V^P, so v ∈ V^B is P-fixed iff T_{s_k}v = qv.
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-CLOZEL-THORNE-17.

items.name: Duality for the localisations of Y
items.statement: If Y_K is self-dual there is a perfect pairing on Y^B_O with ⟨tx, y⟩ = ⟨x, ȷ(t)y⟩, and Y(χ̄ȷ) is the annihilator of ⊕_{η ≠ χ̄} Y(η).
items.locator: Before Proposition 2.9, accepted manuscript p. 18 (using Theorem 3.3)
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-CLOZEL-THORNE-17.

items.name: The Jacquet module of the U(4) packet
items.statement: St₃ ⊞ St₁ on GL₄(E) has Jacquet exponents [1,0,−1,0], [0,1,0,−1] and 2[1,0,0,−1]; it is the unique irreducible submodule of the principal series induced from [1,0,0,−1] ([Pro98]), the only θ-stable exponent being [1,0,0,−1]. The U(4) packet {π₄^±} with stable base change μ^{−1}(St₃ ⊞ St₁) consists of discrete series with Jacquet module 2μ^{−1}(z₁z₂) ⊗ [1, 0] (Mœglin).
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-CLOZEL-THORNE-17.

items.name: The Jacquet form of the endoscopic identity (3.7)
items.statement: For f with orbital integrals supported on the regular part of T_G, ⟨tr π, f⟩ = ∫_{T⁺} Θ(π^norm_{N₀})(t)D_G(t)O_t(f) dt ((3.8), after [CT15, §3.7]), and the endoscopic identity (3.7) gives Σ_{π∈Π_φ} ε(π)·j(π) = 2Σ_w w([k−2, …, 1, 1, 0]), w over the shuffles in S_k increasing on {1, …, k−2} and {k−1, k}; for m = 5 this equals jY′ − jX′ + jZ′.
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-CLOZEL-THORNE-17. The engine of Theorem 3.3; the review checked the shuffle identity against Theorem 2.3's data for k = 3, …, 8.

items.name: The Kazhdan–Lusztig modules X′, Y′ lie in Π_φ
items.statement: The tempered modules X′, Y′ of Theorem 2.5 have semistable stable base change, whose θ-stable exponent [k−2, …, 0, −1, 0, 1, 0, …, 2−k] forces the parameter ⊕ sp(n_i) ⊗ χ_i to have trivial χ_i and {n_i} = {m, 3, 1}; hence X′, Y′ belong to the L-packet of Theorem 3.2.
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-CLOZEL-THORNE-17.

items.name: Archimedean spectral transfer for the compact unitary group
items.statement: At an infinite place, ⟨Θ_{φ_v,H}, f_v^H⟩ = det(w)⟨Θ_C, f_v⟩ for G(F_v) compact and ⟨tr π(H), f^H_{*,∞}⟩ = det(w)⟨a_{wτ}, s⟩ on G* (Kottwitz–Shelstad; [Clo11, Theorem 3.4]); pseudo-coefficients of the trivial-infinitesimal-character packet are associated to the constant 1.
items.locator: §3.3 and proof of Theorem 3.8, accepted manuscript pp. 23, 30–31
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-CLOZEL-THORNE-17. ET.4 builds 'the finite-place transfer maps and infinity pseudocoefficients'.

items.name: Galois representations and weak base change for the definite unitary group
items.statement: An automorphic representation of G(A_F) with trivial Σ_∞ has a weak base change to GL_n(A_E) ([Lab11, Theorem 5.1]) and an attached Galois representation ([Gue11, Theorem 2.3 and §2]), used to separate Hecke families and to define the stable base change Π in Proposition 4.1.
items.locator: Proof of Theorem 3.8, pp. 30–31; Proposition 4.1, p. 34
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-CLOZEL-THORNE-17. AG2.2: 'Apply stable unitary base change and endoscopic character identities from ET.4/ET.7a to identify the GL_n parameter'.

items.name: Local packets at split or unramified places are singletons
items.statement: For n odd and φ an unramified tempered conjugate-orthogonal parameter (or at a place split in E), π₀(S_φ/{±1}) is trivial, so the local L-packet has one element; the counts of Theorems 3.8, 3.10 and Lemma 4.4 use this.
items.locator: Proof of Theorem 3.8, accepted manuscript p. 29
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-CLOZEL-THORNE-17. ML.4 plans the Mok classification inputs, 'packets, multiplicities'.

items.name: Semistability of the base change at the places v_i (corrected [CT15, Lemma 4.3])
items.statement: If Σ contributes to S(U_1, O)_m, the local components Π_w of its stable base change at the places above v_0, …, v_s are semistable: from Σ_σ c(σ)⟨tr σ, f_v⟩ = ⟨tr π_w × I_c, f_{E_w}⟩ with c(σ) > 0 and the twisted Jacquet trace.
items.locator: Proof of Proposition 4.1, accepted manuscript p. 35
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-CLOZEL-THORNE-17. The paper's correction of the proof of [CT15, Lemma 4.3], previously only in item 032's note.

items.name: Preliminary reductions and data for Theorem 5.1
items.statement: After a soluble base change one may assume: (1) there is an everywhere unramified, regular algebraic, conjugate self-dual, ι-ordinary Π′ with r̄_ι(Π′) ≅ r̄_ι(Π); (2) the places above l and below the ramification of Π split in E, with [F_v : Q_l] even for v | l; (3) E/F is everywhere unramified and Π is unipotently ramified; (4) r̄ is trivial at the places above l and at ramified places; (5) [E_w : Q_l] > n(n+1)/2 + 1 and v_l(q_v − 1) > n at ramified v ∤ l. Hence [F : Q] is even and there is a definite unitary group G split by E and quasi-split at every finite place; with the sets V₀, S_a, T, T̃ and the notion of a good extension L (V₀ ∪ S_a split).
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-CLOZEL-THORNE-17. Imports a generalisation of [CHT08, Lemma 4.4.1] and [CT15, §3.3].

items.name: Thorne 2015 inputs for Lemma 5.3 and the choice of D₀
items.statement: (1) The auxiliary problems S₁, S₂ of the proof of Lemma 5.3: the reduction of the reducible universal deformation is r₁ ⊕ r₂ with r_i of type S_i via Λ_{1,L} ⊗̂ Λ_{2,L} ≅ Λ_L, R_{S_i} is finite over Λ_{i,L} of dimension 1 + n_i[L⁺ : Q], and R_{S₁} ⊗̂ R_{S₂} → C is surjective (arguing as in [Tho15, Theorem 7.1], using hypothesis (4) of Theorem 5.1); R_{S_i} ≅ R_{S_i,ψ_i} ⊗̂ O⟦Δ/(c+1)⟧ for l ∤ n_i ([Tho15, Lemma 3.36]). (2) The existence of a good L₀ and D₀ = (L₀, {R^m_v}_{v∈R}) with [L⁺_{0,v} : Q_l] > n² and d_{D₀} > n² + 1 (as in [Tho15, §7]). (3) The rings R_{D^χ₀}/λ and modules S_{D^χ₀}/λ are canonically identified as χ varies ([Ger, Lemma 2.2.6]). (4) R^{χ_v,nil}_v is a domain when the χ_{v,i} are pairwise distinct ([Tho12, Proposition 3.16]).
items.locator: Proofs of Lemmas 5.3 and 5.5 and of Theorem 5.1, accepted manuscript pp. 40–43
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-CLOZEL-THORNE-17. Imported from Thorne 2015, Thorne 2012 and Geraghty; routed with item 039.

items.name: Soluble base change and descent for GL_n
items.statement: For a soluble extension E′/E of CM (or totally real) fields and an irreducible ρ with ρ|G_{E′} automorphic, ρ is automorphic; and cuspidal representations of GL_{r+1}(A_E) invariant under Gal(E/F) descend ([AC89]).
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-CLOZEL-THORNE-17. ML.5 registers cyclic base change; ET.7a develops 'cyclic automorphic-induction/base-change steps from the Arthur–Clozel … proofs'. Item 047 covers only the cuspidality statement [AC89, Theorem 3.4.2].

items.name: Reduction of Theorem 6.1 to Theorem 6.2
items.statement: 'By a series of reductions which are essentially the same as those of [CT15, §6]', Theorem 6.1 follows from Theorem 6.2: after soluble base change and congruences one may assume π ι-ordinary of weight zero, with large residual image and adequacy, and Steinberg at a place u₀ with q_{u₀} a primitive root mod l.
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-CLOZEL-THORNE-17. On the critical path to Theorem 1.1 and given only by reference; routed with the endpoints, as the analogous Clozel–Thorne reductions are in PAPER-NEWTON-THORNE-26 (ct14-ct17-reductions).

items.name: Coefficient conjugates of RACSDC representations are automorphic
items.statement: For a RACSDC Π and γ ∈ Aut(C) there is a RACSDC γΠ with finite part γΠ^∞, and r_ι(γΠ) ≅ r_{γ^{−1}ι}(Π); in particular φr_ι(π) is automorphic for φ an arithmetic Frobenius acting on coefficients (Clozel).
items.locator: Proof of Theorem 6.2, p. 46 (applying [Ram00, Theorem M] to φr_ι(π′_2)); §1, p. 2
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-CLOZEL-THORNE-17. Used without citation. As PAPER-NEWTON-THORNE-26 (conjugation-preserves-automorphy, coefficient-conjugation-galois), routed to AutomorphicGaloisRepresentationsPartII.

items.name: Dickson's classification of finite subgroups of PGL₂(F̄_l)
items.statement: A finite subgroup of PGL₂(F̄_l) is conjugate to PSL₂(F_{l^a}) or PGL₂(F_{l^a}), or is dihedral, cyclic, contained in a Borel subgroup, or isomorphic to A₄, S₄ or A₅.
items.locator: Proof of Lemma 7.5, accepted manuscript p. 48
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-CLOZEL-THORNE-17. R01.4 proves 'the finite-subgroup facts of GL₂/PGL₂ used in the source arguments'.

items.name: Fontaine–Laffaille description of residual inertia
items.statement: For l unramified in F and a crystalline representation with Hodge–Tate weights in an interval of length < l − 1, (r̄|_{I_v})^ss is a sum of powers of fundamental characters determined by the weights ([FL82, §§4–5]).
items.locator: Proof of Lemma 7.5, accepted manuscript p. 48
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-CLOZEL-THORNE-17. R07.3 constructs Fontaine–Laffaille theory and 'how torsion subquotients and reductions change the filtration'; R01.2 the fundamental characters.

items.name: The odd extension R̄ of r̄_ι(Π) ⊗ φ
items.statement: For Π RACSDC of GL₂(A_E) with large residual image there is a continuous φ : G_E → F̄_l^× with (r̄_ι(Π) ⊗ φ)^c ≅ r̄_ι(Π) ⊗ φ, and r̄_ι(Π) ⊗ φ extends to an odd R̄ : G_F → GL₂(F̄_l) (cf. the proof of [Tho15, Theorem 8.1]).
items.locator: Proof of Proposition 7.6, accepted manuscript p. 49
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-CLOZEL-THORNE-17.

items.name: Not CM-induced is equivalent to Sym²π cuspidal for discrete series at infinity
items.statement: For F totally real and π cuspidal on GL₂(A_F) with π_∞ essentially square-integrable, π is automorphically induced from a quadratic CM extension iff it is induced from some quadratic extension iff Sym²π is not cuspidal: induction from K gives a principal series at every real place split in K.
items.locator: Proof of Theorem 7.1, accepted manuscript p. 49
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-CLOZEL-THORNE-17. Used silently: the theorem assumes π not CM-induced, the proof assumes Sym²π cuspidal.

routes.reason: ModularityAndLanglandsExtensions owns the symmetric-power endpoints: ML.0 plans the endpoint and normalisation registry, ML.2 'potential automorphy assembly' and ML.3 'symmetric powers and Sato–Tate', to 'integrate Newton–Thorne source-scoped symmetric-power automorphy' and to 'record weight, level, field and regularity assumptions per source'. The paper's final theorems — Sym^6 and Sym^8 over totally real fields disjoint from Q(ζ_5), Q(ζ_7) (Theorem 6.1), the list of Corollary 7.2 and the holomorphy of L(Sym^n π, s) — are such endpoints under their own hypotheses, and the §7 reductions (Theorem 7.1, Lemmas 7.4–7.5, Proposition 7.6, with the BLGGT14 potential automorphy inputs) are generic symmetric-power arguments ML.3 needs for any source. The level-raising method that proves Theorem 6.2 is not an endpoint and goes to the Part II. Review: accepted. The reduction of Theorem 6.1 to Theorem 6.2 (by reference to [CT15, §6]), the odd extension of Proposition 7.6 and the silent equivalence in Theorem 7.1 were added. BLGGT14 Theorem 4.2.1 and potential diagonalisability moved to route 5 (item 058), since the Newton–Thorne reviews give them one owner there; Theorems 4.4.1 and 5.5.2 stay here as potential automorphy inputs (ML.2).

SR.2 plans Jacquet functors and SR.3 admissible representations, so Casselman's description of the B- and P-invariants through Jacquet modules (Lemma 2.1) is a source there; the Borel–Casselman bijection (SR.1) and the notation of §1.1 (SR.2) are named as planned items. The paper adds a deformation condition in exactly that direction: R^m_v, the O-flat reduced quotient of R^1_v whose Frobenius characteristic polynomial lies in Taylor's Pol_n(m, q_v) for a partition m (monodromy bounded by m), and Lemma 5.2 on its smooth points and minimal primes. These are local statements reusable by any level-raising argument. Review: accepted; L7 plans 'semistable, Steinberg and minimally ramified analogues away from p for rank n, preserving the nilpotent monodromy operator'.
