routes.title: Modularity, automorphy and Langlands endpoint extensions, Part II: symmetric power functoriality by level-raising on definite unitary groups
routes.brief:
Final theorems (Clozel–Thorne, Level-raising and symmetric power functoriality III, Duke Math. J. 166 (2017) 325–402): Theorem 6.2 — for l ∈ {5, 7}, F totally real and (π, χ) RAESDC on GL_2(A_F) ι-ordinary of weight zero, with ρ̄ = r̄_ι(π) of image containing SL_2(F_{l^a}) (a > 1), (φρ̄ ⊗ ρ̄) and Sym^{l−3} ρ̄ adequate on G_{F(ζ_l)}, and a place u_0 ∤ 2 where π is an unramified twist of Steinberg with q_{u_0} a primitive root mod l and ρ̄ ramified, Sym^{l+1} ρ is automorphic; Theorem 4.2 — level-raising on the definite unitary group in l + 2 variables for l = 5, 7; Theorem 5.1 — level-raising to Steinberg for residually reducible RACSDC representations with a Jordan block longer than n_1; Theorem 5.7 — automorphy lifting for ρ with ρ̄ = ρ̄_1 ⊕ ρ̄_2 given an automorphic lift with such a Jordan block.

Cover, in order: (i) the ramified unitary group U_{2k+1}: its Iwahori–Hecke algebra H_B, the isomorphism with that of Sp_{2k} (Proposition 2.2), the parameter φ_E of St_{n−4} ⊞ St_3 ⊞ St_1 and the Iwahori-spherical modules X, Y, Z constructed by Kazhdan–Lusztig (Theorem 2.5, with De Concini–Lusztig–Procesi pavings), their integral structures (Reeder's matrices, Proposition 2.6, Corollary 2.8) and the localisations of Proposition 2.9; (ii) the identification of these modules with the Mœglin–Mok L-packet and its signs (Theorems 2.3, 3.3), through the transfer factors of Lemma 3.6 and Mœglin's Proposition 3.7; (iii) compact transfer to the definite unitary group (Theorems 3.8, 3.10) with the Hecke character μ of Lemma 3.4; (iv) algebraic modular forms and the level-raising argument of §4 (Propositions 4.1, 4.3, Lemma 4.4, Theorem 4.2); (v) the deformation-theoretic level-raising of §5 (Lemmas 5.3–5.6, Theorem 5.1) and Theorem 5.7, with Thorne 2015's residually reducible R = T theory as a stated input; (vi) the congruence Sym^{l+1} ≡ (φr̄ ⊗ r̄) ⊕ χ²Sym^{l−3} and Theorem 6.2.

Import, never re-plan: Modularity, automorphy and Langlands endpoint extensions (ModularityAndLanglandsExtensions) ML.4 for Mok's classification (Theorems 3.2, 3.5) and ML.5 for Gelbart–Jacquet, Kim–Shahidi, Kim, Ramakrishnan and Arthur–Clozel; the source route of this extraction into ML.0/ML.2/ML.3, which receives Theorem 6.1, Theorem 7.1, Corollary 7.2 and the §7 reductions; Endoscopic transfer and unitary trace comparison (EndoscopicTransferAndUnitaryTraceComparison) ET.0, ET.1, ET.4, ET.6 and ET.7 for endoscopic data, Langlands–Shelstad transfer factors, the stable and twisted unitary trace formulas, local Langlands for GL_n and unitary base change; Smooth representations of local groups (SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups) SR.1–SR.3 with this extraction's source route (Casselman, Iwahori–Matsumoto, Bernstein–Lusztig, Kazhdan–Lusztig); Reductive groups, Part II (ReductiveGroupsPartII) RG2.2 and RG2.4 for buildings and parahorics of U_n; Automorphic forms on reductive groups (AutomorphicFormsOnReductiveGroups) AF.5 for algebraic modular forms; Automorphic Galois Representations PartII (AutomorphicGaloisRepresentationsPartII) AG2.0, AG2.2 and AG2.5 for r_ι(Π) and local–global compatibility with monodromy; Reusable infrastructure for potential automorphy over CM fields (PotentialAutomorphyInfrastructure) PA.2 for ι-ordinarity; Local Galois deformation rings and their components (LocalGaloisDeformationRings) L7 and R08.2 with this extraction's source route (the rings R^m_v) and Global Galois deformation rings (GlobalGaloisDeformations) G7 for polarized deformation problems. The definite unitary Hecke algebras, ordinary parts and polarized automorphy lifting (Thorne 2012/2017, Geraghty, BLGGT14) should be imported from the Part II PolarizedAutomorphyLifting proposed by the Boxer–Calegari–Gee extraction once it is designed; Thorne 2015 and Theorem 5.7 could equally join that Part II, and the two design jobs should agree which owns them.

Tests: n = 7 and n = 9 (l = 5, 7), where Reeder's explicit matrices of Proposition 2.6 and the Jacquet-module counts of Theorem 2.3 can be checked directly; Remark 4.5's failure of the count for l > 7; the partition rings R^{(n)}_v = R^St_v. The earlier papers of the series (Clozel–Thorne, Compositio 2014 and Annals 2015, for Sym^5 and Sym^7) are prerequisites and would extend this Part II; Newton–Thorne's later proofs for all n (PAPER-NEWTON-THORNE-21, -21-B, -26) belong to ML.3 by another method.

Review of PAPER-CLOZEL-THORNE-17 (REV-PAPER-CLOZEL-THORNE-17). This candidate is now also extended by PAPER-NEWTON-THORNE-21 (Newton–Thorne I, Part II 'Raising the level') and PAPER-NEWTON-THORNE-26 (Thorne 2024: Theorem 6.11, Theorems 7.5–7.6, Proposition 7.4, Corollary 7.2, Lemma 7.3, Theorem 8.1). The owner question the extraction left open is settled as in those reviews: Thorne 2015's residually reducible theory (its deformation and Hecke objects, R = T and automorphy lifting, and the inputs of item 074), ι-ordinarity, [CT14, Lemma 2.6, Proposition 2.9] and BLGGT14 Theorem 4.2.1 are imported from PolarizedAutomorphyLifting (route 5); Theorems 5.1 and 5.7, which are this paper's, stay here. Import the Iwahori–Matsumoto and Bernstein–Lusztig presentations and Kazhdan–Lusztig's classification from SmoothRepresentationsPartIIParahoricCenters (route 6), and the congruence Sym^{l+1} ≡ (φr̄ ⊗ r̄) ⊕ χ²Sym^{l−3} from ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations G7 (route 7). The review added the §2.3 definitions (ȷ, O[Λ], localisations, e_P), the duality for Y, the U(4) Jacquet lemma, the Jacquet form of (3.7), the membership of X′, Y′ in Π_φ, the corrected semistability argument of [CT15, Lemma 4.3] and the preliminary reductions of Theorem 5.1. Respect the corrections in sourceIssues: E3 (X has exponent [1, 0, −1]); E7 (the (10,10) entry of the n = 9 matrix T_{s₂} is −1/(1+q), and the relation for e₁₁ on p. 16 changes with it); E8 (Theorem 2.4(a) needs the tempered form of s); E10 (the induced representation of (3.9) has socle Y ⊕ Z′, so identify Z as the member of {Z, W} embedding in it other than Y); E20 (irreducibility of r_𝔭 needs Clifford theory and n₁ ≠ n₂, not primitivity of r_{𝔭₀}); E21 (Lemma 5.3 is proved only with unipotent conditions at R₀); E22 (Theorem 6.2 must add, or verify, F(ζ_l) ⊄ F(ad ρ̄) for Theorem 5.7(4)); and the misprints E6, E9, E11–E13 and E15–E19.
routes.reason: The paper's method is planned nowhere. It builds Iwahori-spherical representations of ramified unitary groups from Kazhdan–Lusztig and places them in Mœglin–Mok L-packets, counts automorphic representations of a definite unitary group with endoscopic base change, raises the level with algebraic modular forms and a pairing argument, and then raises it to Steinberg with Thorne's residually reducible deformation theory. The atlas has the ingredients it imports (Mok's classification in ML.4, unitary trace formulas in ET.4/ET.7, known transfers in ML.5) but no level-raising for GL_n or unitary groups: the only level-raising layers are ModularCurvesPartII R14.4 (Ihara, GL_2) and consumers of it. Its output is the symmetric-power endpoint of ML.3, so it is new layers in the direction of ModularityAndLanglandsExtensions, as the Boxer–Calegari–Gee extraction did for level-one change of weight (LevelOneCuspidalCohomologyGLn). It is not folded into ML.3, which records endpoints rather than a 50-page proof. Review: accepted. routes.brief: This route coalesces with SmoothRepresentationsPartIIParahoricCenters, proposed by PAPER-KISIN-PAPPAS-18 and extended by PAPER-HE-21 and PAPER-ZHU-17; keep its id, title, parent, area and brief. sourceIssues.locator: Theorem 6.2 and its proof, accepted manuscript pp. 44–46
sourceIssues.printed: Theorem 5.7 now implies that Sym^{l+1}ρ₂|G_{E₀} is automorphic.
sourceIssues.correction: Add to Theorem 6.2 the hypothesis F(ζ_l) ⊄ F(ad ρ̄), or verify it; it holds when [F(ζ_l) : F] > 2, in particular when F ∩ Q(ζ_l) = Q as in Theorem 6.1.
sourceIssues.reason: Theorem 5.7(4) requires E₀(ζ_l) not to be contained in the field cut out by ad of Sym^{l+1}ρ̄₂, which is the field of the projective image of ρ̄ (scalars act by λ^{l+1} on both summands). E₀ is S-split, so this is equivalent to F(ζ_l) ⊄ F(proj ρ̄). By Dickson the projective image is PSL₂ or PGL₂(F_{l^b}), whose largest abelian quotient is Z/2, so the condition can fail only when [F(ζ_l) : F] = 2 and the quadratic subfield of F(proj ρ̄) is F(ζ_l). The hypotheses of Theorem 6.2 do not exclude that case, and the proof does not check it. Theorem 6.1 is unaffected, provided the reductions of [CT15, §6] keep F linearly disjoint from Q(ζ_l).
